title: Jelly Roll's last big band and his death
summary: Garland names the ten or twelve players, with Paul Howard on sax, in the band Morton was forming; it ended when Morton died.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah. We was gonna have an awful band. We had about ten or twelve of us. Let's see. Let's see. Let's see. I start the name. We had Buster Wilson on piano. Mmhmm. Buster Scott on guitar. I was on the bass. We had a... We had a... Mutt on trumpet. We had an Orion trombone. Mmhmm. Mmhmm.
Quality Serenaders. Mmm. He had a good band, didn't he?
We're about to run out of...
This is the third reel. What were we talking about? We were talking about Johnny Roll Morton's band there, and they had Paul Howard on saxophone.

Well, I guess Bill Russell got that from Paul Howard, because he saw him out there. And it'll come back to him, because he was right there in the section. That would help. Well, whatever happened to that band?
Oh, that band. That band. The band you mean Jelly Roll? Yeah. Well, Jelly Roll died.
And that was the end of that?
That was the end. You know, he was getting that band together. It was something big, I think, in either records or something. I don't know. It was something in New York somewhere.
Oh, Lord. He must have been well-connected then, I'm sure.
Yeah, this was going to be a big thing.
